findings.recommendation: When a merchant's endpoint returns a 5xx or refuses connections, the loop fires the next attempt immediately: the five POSTs land back-to-back, so a merchant that is briefly down or overloaded is hammered, a few seconds of outage exhausts every attempt and the event is dropped, and a burst of payments turns into a retry storm against the merchant's server. Wait between attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (for example 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s), or hand failed deliveries to a delayed retry queue so the wait does not hold the payment listener. Being bounded and idempotent (x-event-id) is not enough: the attempts must also be spaced.
findings.title: Failed deliveries are retried back-to-back, with no backoff

findings.recommendation: When a merchant's endpoint stays down, the event is given up after five attempts and the only trace is a `console.debug` line that bypasses the project's structured logger (src/logger.ts, shipped to the log platform) and is usually filtered out in production; the listener also ignores `deliver` returning false. Lost payment notifications go unnoticed and a merchant's report of a missing webhook cannot be diagnosed. Use `logger.warn` per failed attempt and `logger.error` when the event is dropped, with fields such as `eventId`, `paymentId`, `attempt`, `status` and `error` (not the full webhook URL if it may carry a merchant secret), and act on the false return in the listener.
findings.title: Dropped webhooks are logged only at debug level, in free text

findings.recommendation: When a merchant's endpoint answers 404, 401 or 500, nothing is logged for that attempt (the catch only runs on network errors and timeouts) and the final "dropped" line carries no status: an operator cannot tell a misconfigured URL from a merchant outage, and permanent client errors burn all five attempts. On a non-ok response, log the attempt with `response.status`, and retry only statuses worth retrying (408, 429, 5xx), giving up at once on other 4xx.
findings.title: Non-2xx responses are retried without recording their status
